issues.legal_issue: An unconfirmed auction of secured property does not satisfy a final conditional pre-deposit requirement, and the borrower cannot collaterally challenge that requirement in a later appeal.
material_facts: The appellate tribunal had conditionally stayed enforcement proceedings on the borrowers’ depositing an amount, and the High Court and Supreme Court had rejected the borrowers’ challenge to that order.
The recovery tribunal had specifically found that the bank was entitled to claim the outstanding debt with future interest.
The secured properties were auctioned, but the sale remained subject to confirmation by the appellate tribunal, which had not confirmed it.
The High Court later treated the auction as satisfying the earlier deposit requirement.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s declaration that the deposit requirement had been satisfied. The borrowers were required to comply with the deposit order, failing which their appeal would stand dismissed and the bank could recover the outstanding dues.
issues.legal_principle: Under the second proviso to Section 18(1) of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, an appeal is subject to the prescribed pre-deposit requirement. A conditional order imposing that requirement, after its challenge has been rejected, cannot be indirectly questioned in a later appeal. A sale that remains unconfirmed does not establish that the required deposit has been made.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_deemed_deposit_compliance and prior_conditional_deposit_order_final and tribunal_found_amount_due and auction_sale_unconfirmed

predicates.appeal_challenges_deemed_deposit_complia: A party appealing against an enforcement-related decision challenges a ruling that a required deposit has been satisfied.
predicates.prior_conditional_deposit_order_final: A tribunal imposed a conditional deposit requirement, and a challenge to that order was rejected.
predicates.tribunal_found_amount_due: The tribunal made a specific finding that the creditor was entitled to claim an outstanding debt.
predicates.auction_sale_unconfirmed: Secured property was auctioned, but the sale had not been confirmed by the authority whose confirmation was required.

issues.definition: When a party challenges a finding of deposit compliance after a final conditional deposit order, a finding of debt due, and an unconfirmed auction, the deposit requirement remains unsatisfied.

issues.legal_issue: A borrower who knowingly accepted financing terms and did not previously challenge them cannot invoke the doctrine of unconscionable contract at the enforcement stage to frustrate recovery.
material_facts: The borrowers signed the financing agreements and accepted the loan and other financial facilities on the agreed terms.
They had enjoyed those facilities for more than a decade without challenging the terms.
The court found that the borrowers were not in a position of disadvantage in relation to the bank.
issues.conclusion: The borrowers could not rely on the doctrine of unconscionable contract to resist the bank’s recovery action.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished Central Inland Water Transport Corporation v. Brojo Nath Ganguly and Delhi Transport Corporation v. D.T.C. Mazdoor Congress, holding that the doctrine of unconscionable contract could not be invoked in these circumstances by borrowers who accepted the financing terms with open eyes and were not disadvantaged. The challenge arose in the context of enforcement under Sections 13(2) and 13(4) of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002.

rule.if: borrower_resists_security_enforcement and borrower_accepted_financing_terms_knowingly and terms_not_previously_challenged and borrower_not_disadvantaged

predicates.borrower_resists_security_enforcement: A borrower relies on alleged unfairness of financing terms to oppose a creditor’s security-enforcement action.
predicates.borrower_accepted_financing_terms_knowin: The borrower accepted the financing terms with knowledge of the terms offered.
predicates.terms_not_previously_challenged: The borrower did not challenge the financing terms before the enforcement dispute arose.
predicates.borrower_not_disadvantaged: The borrower was not in a position of disadvantage in relation to the creditor.

issues.definition: If a borrower opposes security enforcement after knowingly accepting unchallenged terms without being disadvantaged, the borrower cannot use unconscionability to frustrate recovery.

issues.legal_issue: A bank may pursue legally permitted recovery measures when a borrower defaults on repayment obligations, including obligations under a compromise that makes the full debt recoverable on default.
material_facts: The parties’ compromise provided that failure to comply with its conditions would entitle the bank to recover the full amount claimed in the recovery proceeding.
The borrowers failed to pay the agreed balance by the stipulated time and paid it only after a substantial delay.
The bank initiated security-enforcement proceedings to recover the outstanding dues.
issues.conclusion: The default entitled the bank to pursue recovery of the outstanding dues, and the small size of the delayed payment did not make the enforcement action unjustified; the bank was entitled and duty-bound to use legally permissible recovery methods.
issues.legal_principle: The Court emphasized that a bank is a trustee of public funds and must seek repayment in accordance with the contract. It referred to the purpose of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, and to Delhi Transport Corporation v. D.T.C. Mazdoor Congress, Central Bank of India v. State of Kerala, and United Bank of India v. Satyawati Tondon. A borrower’s default under a compromise may trigger the agreed entitlement to recover the full debt, and the bank may use legally permissible recovery methods.

predicates.bank_enforces_security_for_defaulted_bor: A bank takes security-enforcement steps to recover money owed by a borrower.
predicates.compromise_restores_full_debt_on_default: The parties agreed that a breach of their compromise would make the full debt recoverable.
predicates.borrower_breached_compromise: The borrower failed to comply with a repayment obligation in the compromise.

issues.definition: When a bank enforces security after a borrower breaches a compromise that restores the full debt, the bank may pursue lawful recovery of the outstanding debt.

issues.legal_issue: A direction for time-bound disposal of pending recovery proceedings should not be disturbed where no valid ground for interference is shown.
material_facts: A recovery application and a related interlocutory application remained pending before the tribunal.
The High Court directed the tribunal to dispose of those matters within a fixed time.
The Supreme Court found no valid ground to interfere with that direction.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal challenging the time-bound disposal direction, leaving it in place.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that it found no valid ground to interfere with the High Court’s direction for time-bound disposal. It did not rely on a specific statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

rule.if: recovery_proceeding_pending and related_interlocutory_application_pending and high_court_directed_time_bound_disposal and no_valid_ground_to_interfere

predicates.recovery_proceeding_pending: A recovery proceeding remains pending before a tribunal.
predicates.related_interlocutory_application_pendin: An interlocutory application related to the recovery proceeding remains pending before the tribunal.
predicates.high_court_directed_time_bound_disposal: The High Court directed the tribunal to dispose of the pending matters within a fixed time.
predicates.no_valid_ground_to_interfere: The appellate court found no valid ground to disturb the High Court’s direction.

issues.definition: When the specified recovery matters remain pending, the High Court has directed their disposal within a fixed time, and no valid ground for interference is shown, that direction stands.
